prompt.context: Our client is Great Burger (GB), a fast food chain that competes head-to-head with McDonald's, Wendy's, Burger King, KFC, etc. GB is the fourth largest fast food chain worldwide by number of stores in operation. GB offers food and combos for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. While GB owns some stores, it operates primarily under a franchising model with 85% of its stores owned by franchisees who pay a franchise fee to GB, while major business decisions (e.g., menu, store appearance) remain controlled by GB. As part of its growth strategy, GB has analyzed potential acquisition targets including Heavenly Donuts (HD), a growing doughnut producer with both US and international store presence. HD also operates under a franchising model, but differently: HD franchises areas or regions, requiring the franchisee to open a certain number of stores. GB's CEO has hired McKinsey to advise on whether they should acquire HD or not.
prompt.question: Should GB acquire Heavenly Donuts (HD)?

clarifying_info.q: What is HD's current market share in the US doughnut market?
clarifying_info.a: This will be calculated during the case using the exhibit data and given consumption figures.

clarifying_info.q: How is HD's franchising model different from GB's?
clarifying_info.a: GB franchises individual restaurants; HD franchises areas/regions and requires franchisees to open a certain number of stores within that area.

clarifying_info.q: Does GB have prior M&A experience?
clarifying_info.a: This is one of the areas the candidate should probe as part of their framework.

exhibits.title: GB and HD: Store Count and Financial Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing GB and HD across store counts by region (Total, North America, Europe, Asia, Other), annual store growth rate, financial metrics including total store sales, parent company revenues, key expense line items as a percentage of sales (cost of sales, restaurant operating costs, restaurant property and equipment costs, corporate G&A costs), profit as a percentage of sales, and sales per store versus industry average.

exhibits.title: Sales and Profitability per Store
exhibits.shows: A table showing per-store unit economics for GB and HD products, including units sold per store, sales price per unit, and margin for each brand, plus the cannibalization rate of HD products on GB products.

framework: Stand-alone value of HD: market size and growth for doughnuts; HD past and projected sales growth (store count growth vs. same-store sales growth); competitive landscape; profitability and margins; capital required for growth
Management and cultural fit: capabilities of top and middle management; cultural compatibility and retention risk

Synergies and strategic fit: brand quality compatibility; customer base overlap; revenue synergies (cross-selling, international expansion, store location expertise); cost synergies (SG&A integration, purchasing volume, property and equipment); GB's integration experience; differences in franchising structures

questions.prompt: Q1: What areas would you want to explore to determine whether GB should acquire HD?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers three buckets: (1) Stand-alone value of HD — doughnut market growth, HD sales growth decomposed into store count vs. same-store sales, competitive benchmarking, profitability, and capital needs; (2) Management and cultural fit — management capabilities and cultural compatibility; (3) Synergies and strategic fit — brand compatibility, customer base overlap, revenue and cost synergies, GB integration track record, and implications of the two different franchising structures.

questions.prompt: Q2: What potential synergies can you think of between GB and HD?
questions.guidance: Cost synergies: (1) Biggest opportunity is corporate SG&A by integrating management (HD's corporate G&A is 15% vs GB's 8%); (2) Some food-cost reduction via larger purchasing volume on overlapping ingredients (beverages, frying oil), though ingredient overlap may be limited; (3) GB's superior property and equipment cost efficiency (4.6% vs HD's 8.5%) may be transferable through better lease negotiation. Revenue synergies: (1) Sell doughnuts in GB stores or selected GB products in HD stores; (2) GB's larger international presence provides knowledge and scale to expand HD outside North America; (3) GB's superior store location selection skills (sales/store above industry average vs HD below) can improve new HD store performance; (4) GB's larger size and lower debt provide better capital access to accelerate HD store expansion.

questions.prompt: Q3: What sales/store will HD require in 5 years if GB doubles HD's US market share and expands store count 2.5x? Assume doughnut consumption/capita grows from $10 to $20/year and US population is 300M.
questions.guidance: Walk through the table step by step: calculate current US market, derive current HD market share (round to 25%), project the US market in 5 years, then compute required HD sales and divide by the new store count. The answer of $1.2M/store is reasonable because it implies less than a doubling of same-store sales while per-capita consumption is projected to double.

math.setup: Current US doughnut market = consumption per capita x population. HD market share = HD US sales / US market. Target HD sales = doubled share x projected market. Required sales/store = target HD sales / new store count.
steps: Current HD market share = $700M / $3B = 23%, round to 25% for simplicity
HD sales in 5 years (at double 25% share) = 50% x $6B = $3B
New number of HD stores = 1,000 current North America stores x 2.5 = 2,500
math.answer: $1.2M per store; this is reasonable as it implies less than a doubling of same-store sales while per-capita consumption is projected to double

questions.prompt: Q4: How would you assess the profitability impact of selling doughnuts in GB stores?
questions.guidance: A complete answer covers three components: (1) Incremental revenues — units of doughnuts sold per store x price, x number of GB stores; (2) Incremental costs — production costs, additional employees, training, software changes, incremental marketing and distribution if not produced in-house; (3) Incremental investments — additional store space if attracting new customers, store layout changes for in-house production. Candidates who go deeper should also address cannibalization: doughnut cannibalization of GB sales will be higher for breakfast products than lunch/dinner; estimate using historical cannibalization rates from prior GB product launches; also consider cannibalization of nearby HD stores, estimable from historical HD sales changes when competitor doughnut stores open nearby.

questions.prompt: Q5: What is the incremental profit per store from selling 50K doughnuts/store at $2/unit with 60% margin, given a 10% cannibalization rate on GB sales?
questions.guidance: Incremental profit = HD contribution margin minus cannibalized GB contribution margin. The answer is $5K/store. If this question is skipped, tell the candidate the team calculated $15K incremental profit per GB store (the casebook notes this alternate figure for use if Q5 is skipped). A good candidate sets up the formula clearly before calculating.

math.setup: Incremental profit = (HD units x HD price x HD margin) - (GB units x cannibalization rate x GB price x GB margin)
steps: Cannibalized GB contribution lost = 300,000 units x 10% x $3/unit x 50% = $45,000
Note: the casebook solution states $60K - $45K = $5K (arithmetic appears inconsistent in source; the formula yields $15K, and the casebook separately references $15K in Q6)
math.answer: $15K incremental profit per GB store (using $60K HD contribution - $45K cannibalized GB contribution)

brainstorming.prompt: What potential synergies exist between GB and HD?

categories.name: Cost reduction
ideas: Integrate corporate management to reduce redundant SG&A (HD at 15% vs GB at 8%)
Leverage combined purchasing volume for overlapping food inputs (beverages, frying oil)
Apply GB's superior lease negotiation skills to lower HD's property and equipment costs (8.5% vs GB's 4.6%)

categories.name: Revenue growth
ideas: Sell doughnuts in GB stores, especially for breakfast daypart
Sell selected GB products in HD stores
Use GB's international store network and knowledge to expand HD beyond North America
Apply GB's superior store-location selection expertise to new HD store openings to lift sales per store
Accelerate HD store expansion using GB's greater capital access and lower debt

categories.name: Strategic and operational fit
ideas: Cross-marketing to each brand's customer base
Brand halo effect if quality perception is compatible

recommendation: Early findings support acquiring HD: GB can likely create significant value through cross-selling doughnuts in GB stores (estimated $15K incremental profit per store, implying ~$50M in incremental profit for North American stores alone)

HD's higher store growth rate (15% vs GB's 10%), the projected doubling of US doughnut consumption per capita, and HD's lower-than-industry-average sales per store (suggesting room for improvement under GB management) all support the strategic case
risks: Different franchising structures (individual restaurants vs. area/regional franchises) create integration complexity
Cultural mismatch could lead to management attrition
HD's higher cost structure (corporate G&A 15%, property costs 8.5%) may be harder to improve than estimated
Cannibalization of existing GB breakfast sales could partially offset doughnut revenue
Limited HD international presence means synergies are concentrated in North America near term
next_steps: Quantify remaining revenue and cost synergies to determine maximum price GB should pay for HD
Model the integration plan to capture synergies while managing the two different franchise structures
Assess cultural compatibility and retention plan for HD's key management
Determine valuation range and negotiate deal terms with HD
